name: Tesla
author: Jankees van Woezik
description: Your Tesla in the bar: where it is, how full it is, how far that gets you, and what you can tell it to do

barWidget.description: Your Tesla in the bar: where it is, how full it is, how far that gets you, and what you can tell it to do

schema.label: VIN
schema.description: Which car is initially selected when the account has more than one. Empty picks the first one Tesla lists. Cars can then be switched from the panel.

schema.label: Show the range in the bar
schema.description: Shows the remaining range as the bar item, just the number in whatever unit the car's own screen uses, instead of the Tesla mark. It is the last reading the panel holds, so it asks the car for nothing extra; off gives you the bare mark. Right-click the widget to toggle it; that choice is remembered.

schema.label: Controls
schema.description: What the panel will let you tell the car to do. Every control wakes the car, because a command is answered by the car itself and a sleeping one cannot hear it — that is the opposite of how the readings work, and it is the right way round for something you pressed on purpose. Essentials is locking, sentry, climate, the windows, the boot and the lights. Everything adds charging, the seat heaters, dog and camp mode, valet and HomeLink. Off leaves the panel as something that only looks.

schema.label: Map
schema.description: Tiles come from OpenStreetMap, which needs no account. It ships one style and it is a pale one, so Dark is that same map inverted and turned half a colour wheel, the way OpenStreetMap's own site does its dark mode: water stays blue, parks stay green, and the paper goes black. Auto follows your theme, because a light map inside a dark panel is a torch in the face and a dark one inside a light panel is a hole in it.

schema.label: Zoom
schema.description: 16 shows the street the car is on and the ones either side, which is the level at which you can tell whether it is where you left it. Lower to see which town, higher to see which parking space.

schema.label: Panel width
schema.description: In the shell's spacing units. The map is this wide and everything else is measured off it, so this one number sizes the whole panel. Anything wider than the screen is trimmed to fit.

schema.label: Look the position up by name
schema.description: Turns the coordinates into a street and a town, through OpenStreetMap's Nominatim. Answers are cached per position, so a parked car is one lookup however often you look at it. Off if you would rather nothing but Tesla learned where the car is.

schema.label: Check whether the car is awake every
schema.description: Minutes. This is the cheap question: Tesla answers it from its own records and the car is never involved, so it costs the car nothing at any interval. It is what lights the bar icon.

schema.label: Leave a parked car alone for
schema.description: Minutes. Reading a car that is awake resets its sleep timer, and a car whose timer keeps resetting never sleeps and flattens its battery over a week of standing still. Tesla needs roughly fifteen minutes of quiet, so shorter than that is the setting that costs you range. A car that is driving or charging is exempt: it is awake regardless.

schema.label: Where a click on the map goes
schema.description: The address opened when you click the map, with {lat} and {lon} standing in for the position. Google Maps by default because that is what most people navigate with; https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat={lat}&mlon={lon}#map=17/{lat}/{lon} keeps it in OpenStreetMap.
